topics.title: The AI job gap isn't coming — it's already 19% wide for workers under 25
topics.why: Stanford's Digital Economy Lab just quantified it: entry-level workers in AI-exposed jobs are falling behind similarly-aged peers by nearly a fifth, and the gap is widening, not stabilizing.

topics.title: 41% of employers say they're planning AI-driven layoffs — but not the ones you'd expect
topics.why: A new employer survey shows workforce cuts targeting automatable tasks rather than whole job categories, which changes what "AI-proofing" your role should actually mean.

topics.title: Enterprise AI hit production this year. Nobody agrees it's working.
topics.why: 97% of executives say they've deployed AI agents, but only 12% of CEOs report AI delivering measurable financial return — the disconnect is where the opportunity for AI-literate operators sits.

topics.title: The AI trainer gig economy just split into two tiers
topics.why: Domain-expert evaluation work (lawyers, doctors, engineers) is paying $80-200/hr while generalist tasks flatten out — the ladder up is now specialization, not just signing up.

topics.title: Agent security is becoming a full-time job before agents even ship
topics.why: Google Cloud and others are pushing "secure-by-default" agent frameworks as the new gating requirement for autonomous AI — an emerging specialty most job seekers haven't noticed yet.
